description: Fill autumn leaf heaps with a continuous sloping material, detailed exterior leaf cards and a gradual circular ground transition while preserving native placement.
changes: Replace open horizontal interior sheets with an opaque sloping surface and filled centre
Use a detailed pile-only atlas with binary alpha and five exterior leaf colours
Flare the lower surface and add a circular ground carpet plus ten lower-half leaf overlays
Keep approved 1/2/3 widths and depths, 0.6/1.2/1.8 heights, item IDs, hitboxes and all Java classes unchanged
advantages: No open horizontal tiers in inspected native views
Leaf silhouettes remain readable and the lower surface joins a dedicated ground layer
Compatibility with user-approved 1.13.0 placement code is preserved byte-for-byte
disadvantages: Final Hytale client visual acceptance remains pending
Generated carpet colour counts approximate the palette rather than proving an exact per-leaf ratio
L uses 250 native nodes out of the verified 255-node limit; additions require budgeting
test_results: Native Blockbench S/M/L imports and oblique/low/side views inspected
Asset bounds, UVs, binary alpha, ground height, central-body opacity and node budgets passed
24 Java classes byte-identical to 1.13.0; only pile visuals/reference and manifest changed
Installed and distribution JAR hashes match; Hytale closed; no production world edits
